design_promise: Choose a commander, open a coherent pack, arrange a readable keep, and adapt when a forecasted invasion tests the doctrine you chose.

p1_content_and_replayability.guardrail: scenario objectives and counter meanings remain stable while target priority or resource pressure may vary

p3_focus_and_response.determinism_rule: focus, hit-testing, preview, and selection order do not mutate authoritative battle outcomes

initial_real_time_auto_battle.ammunition: finite_rounds_for_ranged_pieces; reload at recovery transition; melee uses none

p8_authored_events.command_boundary: choose_event_option validates the complete choice before applying typed effects
p8_authored_events.persistence: active event, resolved IDs, flags, and event history remain authoritative in schema-4 state

p10_accessibility_preferences.determinism_rule: preferences remain outside PackKeepState serialization and never change battle outcomes
p10_accessibility_preferences.persistence: versioned atomic user settings with safe defaults for malformed or future files

p10_controller_and_scaling.input_rule: named actions preserve keyboard and controller paths; rebinding one device family preserves the other

vertical_slice.design_goal: Prove that pack choice and spatial composition are more interesting than a large roster or a mandatory opening build.
vertical_slice.battle_model: deterministic six-step auto-battle with forecast, approach, contact, intervention, adaptation, and outcome phases

unit_roles.name: Frontline
unit_roles.question: Where will pressure be held?
unit_roles.strength: Buys time at a chosen boundary.
unit_roles.weakness: Can be bypassed, surrounded, or made irrelevant by a different approach.

unit_roles.name: Support
unit_roles.question: What makes the rest of the keep recoverable?
unit_roles.strength: Repairs, reinforces, or improves nearby pieces.
unit_roles.weakness: Usually fragile and valuable to sabotage.

unit_roles.name: Control
unit_roles.question: Which space should become dangerous or slow to cross?
unit_roles.strength: Shapes enemy movement and buys time without being a wall.
unit_roles.weakness: Needs sightlines and can restrict friendly movement.

unit_roles.name: Recon
unit_roles.question: Where will information matter soon enough to act?
unit_roles.strength: Reveals threats and improves response timing.
unit_roles.weakness: Does not stop a threat without a prepared response space.

unit_roles.name: Mobile Response
unit_roles.question: Where can a reserve turn uncertainty into time?
unit_roles.strength: Repositions to the pressure point and rescues threatened rooms.
unit_roles.weakness: Requires open lanes, signals, and command attention.

unit_roles.name: Morale and Signal
unit_roles.question: How does the keep coordinate when the plan changes?
unit_roles.strength: Improves response coherence and protects recovery after a breach.
unit_roles.weakness: Provides indirect value and becomes less useful when isolated.

units.name: Pike Squad
units.purpose: Holds a narrow corridor and becomes stronger when the player commits to one approach.
units.player_readability: A visible line of pikes faces one direction; the squad is clearly strong in a lane and weak outside it.

units.name: Shield Wardens
units.purpose: Creates a flexible anchor that protects adjacent defenders rather than maximizing damage.
units.player_readability: A broad shield arc visibly covers the neighboring tile or room.

units.name: Repair Station
units.purpose: Restores nearby structures during or after pressure.
units.player_readability: Workers, tools, and a short repair radius show exactly what the station can save.

units.name: Fire Team
units.purpose: Controls open space by creating a temporary denial zone.
units.player_readability: The denial zone is painted on the ground before placement and remains visible during the wave.

units.name: Scout Post
units.purpose: Reveals approaching doctrine and improves the time available to respond.
units.player_readability: A cone of revealed approach and a countdown show the information gained.

units.name: Runner Pair
units.purpose: Moves between rooms to carry repair kits, signals, or emergency orders.
units.player_readability: A visible route and destination marker show where the runners can reach before the next pressure tick.

units.name: Rear Guard
units.purpose: Turns visible room damage into a stronger second-line response.
units.player_readability: A reserve shield marker changes from RESERVE to ENGAGED after a room is strained.

units.name: Crossbow Patrol
units.purpose: Turns scarce upper-wall space into a readable answer to armored enemies.
units.player_readability: A violet crossbow glyph and bolt trail distinguish the patrol from ordinary ranged defenders.

units.name: Bellkeepers
units.purpose: Turns the keep’s signal network into more reliable coordinated response.
units.player_readability: Signal lines connect the bell to supported rooms and break visibly when a relay is damaged.

units.name: Counter-Siege Team
units.purpose: Creates a deliberate response to large targets without becoming a universal damage solution.
units.player_readability: The firing lane and reload interval are visible before the beast reaches the wall.

equipment.name: Narrow Gate
equipment.purpose: Concentrates pressure into a short lane.
equipment.tradeoff: Improves control at one entrance while reducing flexibility if the threat changes direction.

equipment.name: Wall Brace
equipment.purpose: Reduces breach damage to an adjacent structure.
equipment.tradeoff: Uses space and materials for prevention rather than direct response.

equipment.name: Fire Brazier
equipment.tradeoff: Can make a friendly route unsafe or divide the player’s own response space.

equipment.name: Signal Beacon
equipment.purpose: Improves response time in a connected area.
equipment.tradeoff: Provides no protection when isolated or when the signal path is damaged.

equipment.name: Emergency Shutters
equipment.purpose: Temporarily closes a room or lane to buy time.
equipment.tradeoff: Protects one space while cutting off access and potentially trapping defenders.

equipment.name: Supply Cache
equipment.purpose: Stores a small reserve for repair or evacuation.
equipment.tradeoff: Adds recovery capacity but creates a valuable sabotage target.

equipment.name: Breakaway Barricade
equipment.purpose: Absorbs one dangerous room contact and breaks in the process.
equipment.tradeoff: Consumes space and cannot protect a second impact.

equipment.name: Watch Banner
equipment.purpose: Adds one damage to a nearby ranged defender without attacking itself.
equipment.tradeoff: Uses upper-wall space and materials for a non-stacking support effect.

pack_families.name: Pike Line
pack_families.purpose: Build a strong, readable corridor defense.
pack_families.player_question: Which approach is worth making narrow and strong?
pack_families.strength: Reliable concentrated defense against a declared gate assault.
pack_families.weakness: Loses value when threats spread, bypass walls, or attack support rooms.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: It must not be the mandatory first pick for every scenario.

pack_families.name: Field Engineers
pack_families.purpose: Make the keep recoverable after structural damage.
pack_families.player_question: What can I afford to lose because I prepared a second chance?
pack_families.strength: Makes partial breach survivable and rewards connected support rooms.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: It cannot repair every room during an active wave.

pack_families.name: Firekeepers
pack_families.purpose: Shape open space into a temporary denial zone.
pack_families.player_question: Which empty space should become expensive to cross?
pack_families.strength: Punishes open approaches and gives mobile defenses time.
pack_families.weakness: Needs clear sightlines and can deny friendly movement.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: It is not a universal answer to siege beasts or sealed rooms.

pack_families.name: Scouts
pack_families.purpose: Reveal the threat early enough for the keep to respond.
pack_families.player_question: Where will earlier knowledge create an actual response?
pack_families.strength: Improves forecasts and creates time for deliberate intervention.
pack_families.weakness: Does not help a keep with no reserve, space, or command points.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: Information cannot replace a defense plan.

pack_families.name: Shieldwall
pack_families.purpose: Create a resilient anchor and a controlled retreat.
pack_families.player_question: Which boundary can protect the rooms behind it?
pack_families.strength: Creates resilient anchors and controlled retreats.
pack_families.weakness: Slow to rotate and vulnerable to distributed sabotage.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: A strong anchor cannot protect disconnected rooms.

pack_families.name: Runner Network
pack_families.purpose: Make open layouts and rapid redeployment viable.
pack_families.player_question: Where should a reserve be able to arrive before the next failure?
pack_families.strength: Makes open layouts and adaptive defense viable.
pack_families.weakness: Needs clear lanes and loses value when signals or morale collapse.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: Movement is not free and cannot save every front simultaneously.

pack_families.name: Fallback Convoy
pack_families.purpose: Hold a second line and spend one structure to save another.
pack_families.player_question: What should remain ready after the first line bends?
pack_families.strength: Reactive defense after visible damage and one controlled sacrifice.
pack_families.weakness: Provides less value before contact and consumes reserve space.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: A fallback cannot rescue every damaged room.

pack_families.name: Crossbow Watch
pack_families.purpose: Build an elevated precision line against armored pressure.
pack_families.player_question: Which upper-wall lane deserves a scarce armor-piercing response?
pack_families.strength: Ignores armor and rewards a compact, readable ranged formation.
pack_families.weakness: Finite ammunition and wall-only placement make it poor at broad or prolonged defense.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: Armor piercing answers Shield Guards but does not replace a complete keep layout.

pack_families.name: Bell Guard
pack_families.purpose: Turn signals and morale into coordinated response.
pack_families.player_question: How will the keep know when to change its plan?
pack_families.strength: Improves pause warnings, morale recovery, and multi-room coordination.
pack_families.weakness: Indirect value and high vulnerability when the signal chain is broken.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: Coordination cannot compensate for an unusable layout.

pack_families.name: Counter-Siege
pack_families.purpose: Prepare a deliberate answer to slow area-pressure threats.
pack_families.player_question: Which large threat is worth reserving space and materials to answer?
pack_families.strength: Provides a deliberate answer to slow area-pressure threats.
pack_families.weakness: Consumes space and is weak against fast or bypassing enemies.
pack_families.does_not_guarantee: It must not become a required late-game pack in every scenario.

enemy_doctrines.question: Can the player concentrate enough strength at the obvious entrance?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: A clear gate marker and a short approach forecast.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Raiders arrive quickly at one pressure point.

enemy_doctrines.question: Can the player protect support pieces instead of only the front wall?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: Several support-room markers with one highlighted likely target.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Sappers split attention and damage a dependency.

enemy_doctrines.question: Has the player left an interior response and clear movement space?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: A false approach marker paired with a wall-bypass warning.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Climbers bypass the strongest front-facing defense.

enemy_doctrines.question: Can the player preserve recovery when several pieces are damaged together?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: A large impact radius and a slow approach from outside the normal lane.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: A siege beast creates structural and movement pressure around one area.

enemy_doctrines.question: Did the keep preserve a reserve after answering the first threat?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: Gate, support, and area-impact markers appear in their expected contact order.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Raiders and a Sapper draw out the first response before a Siege Beast reaches the fallback space.

enemy_doctrines.question: Did the player reserve a precise answer for armor instead of relying on generic damage?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: A red shield marker and visible armor value appear on the gate road.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Shield Guards absorb ordinary contributors while mixed threats punish an overly narrow firing line.

enemy_doctrines.question: Can the player maintain useful information when sightlines are deliberately degraded?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: Smoke corridors and signal interference markers appear before the wave.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Ash slingers reduce visibility and interrupt coordination.

enemy_doctrines.question: Can the keep survive when static protection is explicitly bypassed?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: A heavy hammer marker identifies the strongest frontline target before contact.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Shieldbreakers target the strongest frontline or fortification and ignore adjacent protection.

enemy_doctrines.question: Can the player protect defenders from being worn down while the main attack remains visible?
enemy_doctrines.telegraph: A broad harassment band appears behind the main threat.
enemy_doctrines.pressure_pattern: Skirmishers drain morale and condition without becoming the main target.

enemies.readable_behavior: Takes the shortest declared approach and pressures a gate or exposed entrance.
Moves toward a marked support dependency and damages structures rather than chasing defenders.
Uses a visible wall route to enter a less defended interior space.
Advances slowly and damages several nearby structures on impact.
Advances behind a red shield, displays armor 2, and absorbs damage from every contributor without armor piercing.
Creates a temporary obscured zone that weakens forecasts and signal links.
Avoids the strongest front and harasses exposed defenders or signal pieces.
Targets the strongest frontline piece and visibly ignores adjacent protection.

enemies.name: Burrower
enemies.readable_behavior: Surfaces at a forecasted interior marker rather than following the outer wall.

resources.visibility: Always visible; every cost previews before placement.
resources.design_guardrail: Do not create a second hidden construction currency.

resources.purpose: Pays for pause-sensitive interventions and commander abilities.
resources.visibility: Visible before and during waves; income and spend are logged.
resources.design_guardrail: A player should have at least one meaningful intervention available in the first wave.

resources.visibility: Shown through the bell, defender reactions, and a concise numeric band.
resources.design_guardrail: Morale changes must have a named cause and a recovery route.

resources.purpose: Limits how many doctrines can coexist in one defense.
resources.visibility: A small row of named pack slots, never an endless inventory.
resources.design_guardrail: Limit choices to preserve identity; do not simulate collectible rarity.

within_run_tracks.name: Doctrine Coherence
within_run_tracks.advances_when: Pieces from compatible packs support a readable layout rather than simply being collected.
within_run_tracks.guardrail: Mixed packs remain viable when they solve different problems; no single family should dominate.

within_run_tracks.name: Keep Recovery
within_run_tracks.advances_when: The player repairs, preserves, or deliberately sacrifices a damaged room.
within_run_tracks.guardrail: Recovery should reduce future options or cost resources; it must not erase consequences.

within_run_tracks.name: Invasion Knowledge
within_run_tracks.advances_when: The player correctly reads a forecast or survives a new doctrine.
within_run_tracks.guardrail: Knowledge improves agency, not raw damage.

campaign_progression.principle: Unlock new commanders, packs, rooms, and scenario modifiers through completed objectives and lessons, not repeated grinding.

spatial_rules.rule: All pieces use a snapped grid footprint and cannot overlap.
spatial_rules.player_value: Placement is deliberate and deterministic rather than cursor-sensitive.

spatial_rules.rule: Rooms provide support functions and become meaningful targets when damaged.
spatial_rules.player_value: The keep is a set of priorities, not an abstract board.

spatial_rules.rule: Movement lanes and attack or signal sightlines are previewed before placement.
spatial_rules.player_value: The player can understand why a unit works or fails.

spatial_rules.rule: Some layouts gain value from leaving response space empty.
spatial_rules.player_value: The game rewards restraint and makes the Warden distinct from the Castellan.

spatial_rules.rule: A room or wall can be deliberately closed or abandoned when the player has a visible recovery route.
spatial_rules.player_value: Partial loss becomes a strategic decision instead of a binary failure.

principles: Every new enemy doctrine is taught in isolation before combination.
Every forecast exposes at least one likely target and one uncertainty source.
The player receives a reserve option, redraw, pause intervention, or recovery action before a bad draw can become a forced loss.
Pause and speed controls reduce execution burden; important breaches can trigger optional auto-pause.
A partial breach preserves a playable keep and shortens the next setup rather than restarting a long scenario.
No unit or pack is balanced around co-op coverage or simultaneous multi-player attention.
anti_failure_tests: Can the first wave be survived with either starting commander?
Can every vertical-slice pack answer at least one forecasted doctrine?
Can a player recover after losing the gate or a support room?
Does a compact Castellan layout and an open Warden layout each have a scenario where it is attractive?
Can the player explain why a breach occurred from the map and report?

sample_builds.name: Gatehouse Lock
sample_builds.spatial_idea: Compact gate corridor backed by a repair spine.
sample_builds.weakness: Vulnerable when support rooms or open-yard routes are ignored.

sample_builds.name: Open Yard Net
sample_builds.spatial_idea: Preserved movement lanes with early-warning and denial zones.
sample_builds.strength: Adapts to bypasses and distributed pressure.
sample_builds.weakness: Requires materials discipline and can collapse if morale or signals are cut.

sample_builds.name: Scarred Refuge
sample_builds.spatial_idea: A smaller defended core with an evacuation route through the chapel.
sample_builds.strength: Turns partial breach into a successful refuge outcome.
sample_builds.weakness: Gives up direct defensive power and cannot protect every room.

battle_phases.player_action: inspect doctrine, approach, likely target, and uncertainty
battle_phases.system_action: show counter families before placement locks

battle_phases.player_action: pause between steps and preserve command points

battle_phases.system_action: defenders act, then surviving enemies attack targets
reduce the next room hit and restore placed-piece condition

battle_phases.player_action: repair, rebuild, or accept a partial breach
battle_phases.system_action: award recovery based on held, breached, or collapsed state

enemy_mechanics.target_priority: declared doctrine target, then lowest condition, then stable ID order
enemy_mechanics.health_rule: small health pools; difficulty comes from route, timing, and target choice
enemy_mechanics.telegraph_rule: reveal doctrine, approach, likely target, approximate arrival, and one uncertainty
enemy_mechanics.damage_rule: room damage changes named room functions; piece damage changes condition and can disable a unit
enemy_mechanics.recovery_rule: a single breached critical room is recoverable; collapse requires three critical breaches or zero morale

repair_interval.collapse_behavior: collapse has no repair interval and restarts from preparation
repair_interval.design_purpose: make damage matter without turning recovery into a hidden reset or a second construction phase

room_assignments.effect: denial zone reaches the response space

requirements: siege beast area radius and AREA label
focused enemy double outline and FOCUSED label
focused target line and TARGET label
defeated state disappears from active map

menu_states.purpose: introduce Greywatch and the core promise
choose pack, place pieces, assign rooms, and repair
inspect forecast, enemy actors, and step-by-step contact
read outcome and return to recovery or preparation

unit_availability.gating: only starter pieces and pieces from opened packs may be placed

combat_metrics.resolution: one eligible deterministic attack per unit per battle step
